doc: The pipeline call: float32 s, fine, streak (array) and subtexel (array), float64 threshold column t of shape (h, 1), default GenParams. Covers the shield ramp (both saturations), the shield texture (streak clipped at 0 and at 1), the cumulus density window and the binomial sub-texel term. The output is float64 but numpy rounds 1 + a_fine fine and 0.5 + 0.5 streak to float32 first, so a float64 port differs by those roundings; tolerance is the golden float32 default. Arguments: s, fine, t, streak and subtexel are the inputs of that name when listed; an unlisted t, streak (default 0.0) is the scalar in params, an unlisted subtexel is None; prm holds the GenParams fields compose reads (the others keep their defaults). params.result_dtype ("f64" or "f32") is the dtype numpy gives the result by promotion (a float64 t array or float64 inputs give f64, a python-float t with float32 fields keeps f32); it is informational, the stored output has that dtype. Measured: promoting the float32 inputs to float64 changes the output by at most 5.8e-8; one-ulp nudges of every float input and parameter change it by at most 1.9e-7 (worst of 6 random trials); the tolerance is 14x the larger of the two spreads.
